As someone who knows the industry very well-a couple of things to point out.

First, most companies will charge the rental fee, personally it is preference at that point, but always remember they replace it whatever happens to it and you aren't stuck footing the bill...personally, I like paying my items in full, and would encourage everyone to go out and buy their own.

Second, most modems will need upgrading, especially now they must be 3.0 compatible, but honestly even some of those modems are obsolete that are on the older end...DOCSIS 3.0 started with an 8 downstream bonding, and 4 upstream bonding (lingo-laymans is how it modulates and demodulates-for really laid laymans, how the modem works [MOdulateDEModulate]). Most MSO (major cable companies) are pushing 24 downstreams to bond-also most cable companies are upgrading base speeds and it is necessary if you are wanting higher speeds-which is the push as DOCSIS 3.1 (OFDM technology which changes how downstreams and upstreams are bonded).

Moral of the story, if you buy a modem, and are in a major metropolitan area, and want cable services, buy a DOCSIS 3.1 modem compatible with your provider. The technologies in this industry change, the Modems have to also unfortunately.

On a different note, nice to see after the net neutrality bs that the MSO's are increasing speeds again. Just calling it as I see it, since this industry is my livelihood.
